per_case_results.query: As a central government employee, how is the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation determined?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under the Income-tax Rules, 1962 (Section 17(2)), the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation for a central government employee is determined using Table I (Valuation of Perquisites). For accommodation provided directly by the Central Government or a State Government (Sl. No. (1) in Table 1), the value is calculated as the base value from column (3) plus 10% per annum of the cost of furniture (including televisions, radios, refrigerators, household appliances, air-conditioning plants, or other similar appliances). If the furniture is hired from a third party, the actual hire charges are used instead. Any rent actually paid by the employee is deducted from this value.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: This provision is applicable under the Income-tax Rules, 1962 (Section 17(2)) for the financial year (FY) preceding the assessment year. The effective date of these rules is 1-9-2023 (as indicated in the statutory context). Therefore, this determination method applies to Assessment Years (AY) starting from AY 2021-22 onwards (i.e., for FY 2020-21 and subsequent years).

per_case_results.query: How did the Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption rules change between Rule 2B of the 1962 rules and Rule 278 of the 2026 rules regarding block years?
per_case_results.direct_answer: The main change between the 1962 Rule 2B and 2026 Rule 278 regarding block years is that the 2026 rule explicitly limits the LTC exemption to individuals claiming for two journeys within a block of four calendar years commencing from the calendar year 2022. Under the 1962 rules, the exemption could theoretically apply to any block of four calendar years without such a time-bound restriction. Additionally, the 2026 rules impose additional limitations including a cap on the exemption for children born before October 1, 1998, and restrict the benefit to no more than two surviving children.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Both the 1962 Rule 2B and 2026 Rule 278 are applicable to all financial years (FY) and assessment years (AY) where they were in force. The 2026 rule contains a specific temporal restriction limiting its application to blocks of four calendar years commencing from the calendar year 2022 (i.e., FY 2022-23 and later). The 1962 rule has no such temporal restriction and would apply to all applicable periods.
